newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ahead in Nokia-led trade, eyes on U.S..
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ahead in Nokia-led trade, eyes on U.S..

text.p: Shares ticked ahead in calm post-holiday trade on Friday with Nokia paring early gains but still trading above its previous Helsinki close, brokers said.
Domestic investors were mainly sidelined following the May Day holiday and ahead of the weekend, brokers said.
"For an off day this isn't all that bad," one broker said, referring to the total bourse turnover of 200 million markka.

Nokia, which accounted for over half the volume, was up 3.60 markka at 328.00 after touching 330.50 on an overnight boost from its gains on Wall Street. A Moody's confirmation of Nokia's short-term credit ratings had no share price impact.

Outokumpu traded 0.50 higher at 99.50 after hititng 100.00 in fairly lively 12 million markka volume. Brokers said the share was still being helped by recent news of better prospects for metals prices.
They said Outokumpu may also have drawn strength from the interest in metal shares generated by Rautaruukki's share offering.
Rautaruukki rose 0.90 markka to 46.50, well above its 42.00 per share offering price, in fair nine million markka volume.
PK Cables rose 3.00 markka to a life high 77.00 markka in modest 1.5 million markka trade.
"When Nokia does well, PK Cables should do well too," one broker said, referring to PK Cables' position as a subcontractor to Nokia.
The market would be watching U.S. April payrolls data, due at 1530/1230 GMT for a cue to interest rate trends.
